commentary: Sweden's Spring Economic Bill (HD03100) arrives at a difficult moment: GDP growth of just +0.82% in 2024 and a contraction of –0.20% in 2023 leave Sweden as the weakest performer among Nordic peers — Denmark grew at +3.48% and Norway at +2.10% over the same period. Unemployment has risen to 8.69% in 2025, up from 8.40% in 2024, adding pressure to Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson's credibility claim. The government's fuel tax cut of SEK 0.50–0.80 per litre (HD03236) offers visible consumer relief, but the underlying growth gap narrows its political impact: voters experiencing Sweden's economic underperformance relative to its Nordic neighbours may prove unpersuaded by a single pump-price cut ahead of September's election.
